A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoLM, despite the revised title. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original language-model fine-tuning results, comparisons, convergence measurements, and ablations in Tables 1–7 and Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v3 retains original fine-tuning experiments and adds model evaluations, memory analyses, and pre-training results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: CoLM retains the same source-aware selection, Adam normalization, zeroth-order V-projection gradients, sparsification, and facility-location objective. Algorithm 1 adds explicit gradient-estimation, normalization, and masking steps already described in v2 Sections 4.2–4.3; these are documentation expansions.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds language-model pre-training on five Pile components: EuroParl, GitHub, HackerNews, NIH Exporter, and English Wikipedia. It adds downstream evaluation on SQuAD, WiC, and COPA. This substantially extends training domains and task coverage beyond the retained MathInstruct and classification experiments.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds a low-rank MeZO gradient comparator using GaLore-style SVD projection. The existing actual-gradient, projected-gradient, and MeZO rows are retained with clearer names. The main fine-tuning comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds Llama-3.2-1B/3B and Llama-3.1-8B evaluations, extends batch-size testing, and introduces memory measurements across batch sizes. Appendix F adds a Llama-60M setup with 10K training iterations, 1024-token sequences, held-out perplexity, and downstream accuracy. These are additional experimental settings; the newly disclosed gradient accumulation does not establish a change to retained experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds direct analysis of memory scaling with batch size and selection overhead (Figure 2c and Appendix E), materially strengthening investigation of the central efficiency premise. It also adds training-loss trajectories (Figure 5a) and the low-rank gradient ablation (Table 5). Existing component, sparsity, layer, and completion-length analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are repeated three times and retain the same uncertainty-reporting format for corresponding fine-tuning tables. No new seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or estimation procedures are documented. Revised Table 7 means and uncertainty values are result changes.

E6.justification: v3 adds Llama evaluations, memory and loss results, the low-rank ablation, and pre-training outcomes; Table 9 reports average accuracy 43.9 for CoLM versus 42.5 for larger-batch pre-training. Under the same stated fine-tuning setup, Table 7 changes online-clustering accuracy from 75.8 to 78.7 and fine-tuned-clustering accuracy from 81.9 to 81.0. Reported memory savings versus batch sizes 128/256 change from 2x/4x to 20%/45%. Table 1 accuracy values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Theorems 4.1–4.3, and Appendix A assumptions, lemmas, proofs, and variance-reduction result are unchanged. Moving the small-source definition and expanding pseudocode introduce no new mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and headline claims: source-aware mini-batch coresets, adaptation to Adam and high-dimensional gradients, memory savings, and performance exceeding larger random batches. The expanded model list supplies additional support without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly explains that CoLM reduces activation memory, distinguishing it from weight and optimizer-state savings and explaining why benefits grow with batch size. Appendix D adds a rationale for emphasizing downstream performance over perplexity and explicitly notes MathInstruct's lack of a held-out validation set.

D1.justification: Appendices C/E newly disclose eight-step gradient accumulation, effective-batch accounting, per-device capacity constraints, and an estimated selection overhead below 200 MB. Appendix F and Table 8 document pre-training mixture weights, token chunking, training duration, and hardware. These materially extend reproducibility information, particularly for interpreting the memory comparisons.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for Llama 3, the Pile, SQuAD, WiC, COPA, and the relationship between pre-training loss and downstream performance. GaLore also becomes the basis of an evaluated gradient approximation. The related-work discussion and overall research positioning otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title, adds the conference header, makes localized wording edits, reorders results paragraphs, moves dataset details into the appendix, and exchanges the pseudocode and settings appendix order. Pseudocode explanations expand, but most existing narrative and theoretical text remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 2–3 are substantially reorganized: the model comparison expands, memory displays are added, and existing panels move. v2 Figures 4–5 become the two panels of v3 Figure 4. New Figures 5–6 and Tables 8–9 present supplementary and pre-training material, while Table 5 gains a row. Figure 5b redisplays convergence against training time rather than adding an independent experiment.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the paper's central memory-efficiency evidence. It replaces v2's 4x memory-saving assertion for the main comparison with a quantified 45% reduction, adds memory-scaling and overhead analyses, and discloses gradient accumulation. Additional model and pre-training experiments broaden empirical support. A new Section 5.4 inconsistency remains: the claimed 6.8-point benefit over online clustering is only 2.3 points in Table 7. This localized reporting error does not outweigh the substantial improvement in resource accounting and empirical validation.
